query: A 28-year-old female reports that, for more days than not over the past 3 years, she has felt "down" and, at times, "mildly depressed." Over this period, she also endorses feeling fatigued, difficulty concentrating, and often sleeping more than in the past. The patient denies any manic or hypomanic periods and also reports that she did not have any periods of extreme worsening of her depressed mood beyond that described above. She also denies any suicidal ideation. What is the minimum amount of time this patient must exhibit these symptoms in order to meet the diagnostic criteria for dysthymia?
